observations: Single tire with manufacturer label on tread.
EU energy label visible on the sticker.
Tire appears new with factory markings (blue line) in grooves.
Stack of larger, used-looking tires in the background.

risks.risk: Manufacturing date (DOT code) is hidden; rubber degrades and becomes unsafe over time regardless of tread.
risks.proof: A close-up photo of the DOT code on the sidewall (4 digits in an oval).

risks.risk: Quantity is not specified in text.
risks.proof: A photo of the full set being offered or a written confirmation of quantity.

proof_requests: Photo of the DOT code on the sidewall to verify the year of manufacture.
Confirmation of whether the price is for one tire or a set.
response.reason: The brand, model, and size are clearly visible on the factory label. It can be priced as a single new budget-tier tire, assuming it is old stock until the DOT code is provided.
